sb.topic.start.title: First steps with Second Brain
sb.topic.start:
Second Brain keeps your method, your projects and their memory in plain files, on your disk.
Three places: the terminal; the Pilot, which thinks with you; the Executor, an agent with a shell that measures and does.
Each step says where to type it. A verb is typed sb <verb> in a terminal, /sb:<verb> with the sb plugin, $sb <verb> in Codex.

1. Check the machine	In the terminal: sb doctor
2. Introduce yourself and start an idea: the SB - Accueil Pilot
   get its block	In the terminal: sb pilot-prompt --accueil --copy   (anywhere in your workspace)
   paste it	In your Pilot's host: where pilot-prompt says, Ctrl+V
   then the starting interview	In the Pilot: write hello; it asks, one question at a time, what you do,
   	what matters, your three current headaches; an idea becomes an initiation order there
3. See your projects	In the terminal: sb list
4. Start something new	In the Executor: sb new --order <file>   (the welcome Pilot's order; or sb new, sb adopt)
5. Set up its Pilot	In the terminal: sb pilot-prompt <folder> --copy   then Ctrl+V in the Pilot's host
6. Open a working window	In the Executor, opened in the project's folder: sb open
7. Ask the Pilot for a Mission	In the Pilot: sb mission
8. Run it	In the Executor: sb run <number>
9. Read what came back	In the Pilot: sb relay
10. Close the session	In the Pilot first: sb close; then in the Executor: sb close

Lost at any moment? In the terminal: sb status tells you where you are and what comes next.
sb.topic.concepts.title: Concepts
sb.topic.concepts:
Vault	the Second Brain itself: rules, decisions, skills, tools. One per workspace.
Workspace	the folder that holds the Vault and your projects, marked by VAULT-ROOT.md.
Project	a folder the Vault knows (adopted): its own state, Missions, reports.
Pilot	the window that thinks and decides with you, in a host without a shell (Claude app, Codex, Gemini CLI…).
Host	the software an agent runs in; any host where the Vault's server is declared can play a role.
Executor	the window that measures, executes and proves, in a host with a shell (Claude Code, Codex…).
Mission	the written order the Pilot gives the Executor: context, steps, gates, validations.
Note	the light form: an Owner prompt carried out without a Mission, traced by a Note.
RELAY	the short block that ends every report, carried back from the Executor to the Pilot.
Handoff	a resume note for the next session.
Guardian	a check that runs at each commit and refuses what breaks the rules.
Owner	you: you arbitrate, you push, you delete; agents never do.
sb.topic.scenarios.title: Which window, for which situation
sb.topic.scenarios:
A new idea, no project yet	Pilot « SB - Accueil » (its block: sb pilot-prompt --accueil): think it through; it writes an initiation order
Tell Second Brain who you are	Pilot « SB - Accueil »: the starting interview, then a profile order; Executor: sb profile --order <file>
Create the project from that order	Executor: sb new --order <file>
A folder you already have	Executor, in that folder: sb adopt
Work in an existing project	Pilot « SB - <Name> » + Executor opened in the project folder: sb open
Run a Mission	Executor in the project: sb run <number>
A question, no project	any window: a free session, it answers and writes nothing
A window opened at the workspace root	it refuses to work there: open it in a project folder
A folder not adopted, no order	sb adopt, or ask the welcome Pilot for an order
First installation	the published installation line, then sb doctor

sb.clean.title: Second Brain · what clutters
sb.clean.rule:
sb clean deletes nothing and moves nothing. A move to _trash is prescribed by a Mission;
emptying _trash or the temporary folder is your gesture, when you decide.
sb.install.title: Second Brain · installation
sb.install.pathYes: sb is in your user PATH
sb.install.pathNo: sb is not in your user PATH: sb install --path
sb.install.path.reopen: Open a new terminal for it to take effect.
sb.install.next:
Put sb on the PATH	sb install --path
Repair or resume the installation	sb install --run
See /sb:<verb> in Claude Code (once, your gesture):
  claude plugin marketplace add "{1}"
  claude plugin install sb@second-brain
sb.uninstall.title: Second Brain · uninstall
sb.uninstall.steps:
Nothing is deleted by sb. The steps, yours:
1. Take sb off your PATH: sb uninstall --path   ({1})
2. In Claude Code, if you added it: claude plugin uninstall sb@second-brain
3. Delete the workspace folder when you decide: {0}
The full guide, with the MCP server entry and old profile links:

sb.publish.notLab: this Vault has no release remote: it is not the laboratory.
sb.verb.open.summary: Open a work session and get the READY / NOT-READY verdict
sb.verb.open.doesNot:
It writes nothing, commits nothing. It never opens a session at the workspace root
or in a folder that is not adopted: it tells you where to go instead.
sb.verb.open.examples:
cd C:\Users\you\Workspaces\my-project	go to the project
sb open	measure, then let the agent give the verdict
/sb:open	the same, from Claude Code
sb.verb.close.summary: Close the session: starts in the Pilot, ends in the Executor
sb.verb.close.does:
In the Pilot: the inventory of holes, then the handoff and the closing command — or « nothing to record »
when the session produced no Mission, no RELAY and no artefact (light close).
In the Executor: shows the measured situation (light or full) and each repository's push state;
--light makes the light close; --accueil lists the welcome session's orders.
sb.verb.close.doesNot:
It never pushes: the push is yours, or delegated by you in so many words; the distribution repository
of an installed Vault is never a push target. The Pilot never declares the close done.
sb.verb.close.examples:
sb close	in the Pilot first (as a message), then in the Executor
/sb:close	the same, from Claude Code
sb close --light	in the Executor, when the situation says « light close »
sb close --accueil	at the workspace root, after a welcome session
sb.verb.handoff.summary: Write a handoff for the next session, without closing
sb.verb.handoff.does:
Gives the file name to use (date, time, your slug) and the template;
your agent writes the resume queue from what this session measured.
sb.verb.handoff.doesNot:
No inventory of holes, no journal line, no commit. Committing a handoff
will require its close: that is sb close.
sb.verb.handoff.examples:
sb handoff pause-before-review	propose the file name
/sb:handoff pause-before-review	the agent writes it
sb.verb.status.summary: Where you are, what is pending, what to do next
sb.verb.status.does:
Names the workspace, the Vault and its state, the place you are in; in a project,
its repository, current state, next action, open doors, last handoff, report and Mission.
Ends with the commands that usually come next.
sb.verb.status.doesNot: It changes nothing and runs no check: that is sb doctor.
sb.verb.status.examples:
sb status	anywhere
sb status	as a message to the Pilot: it answers from the digest
sb.verb.help.summary: This screen; sb help <verb> for one command
sb.verb.help.does:
Shows the welcome screen, the page of one verb, or one of three guides:
start, concepts, scenarios. In your language; the verbs stay in English.
sb.verb.help.doesNot: It never runs the verb it describes.
sb.verb.help.examples:
sb help	the welcome screen
sb help open	one verb
sb help scenarios	which window for which situation
sb help --lang es	in Spanish
sb.verb.profile.summary: Show or apply your starting profile
sb.verb.profile.does:
With no argument, shows the « Profil de départ » section of USER.md and the fields it lacks.
With --order, applies the profile order you dated: rewrites that section only,
then files the order in _archive/orders/.
sb.verb.profile.doesNot:
It asks nothing (the welcome Pilot's interview does), touches no other section
of USER.md, commits USER.md alone, and refuses the laboratory Vault's skeleton.
sb.verb.profile.examples:
sb profile	shows the profile and what is missing
sb profile --order _orders/PROFILE-2026-09-27-101500.md	applies the welcome Pilot's order
sb.verb.new.does:
Creates the folder in your workspace with its skeleton, identity, journal, Pilot prompt
and registry line, then prints the block to paste into its Pilot Project.
sb.verb.new.doesNot: It refuses an existing folder (that is sb adopt), the workspace root and the Vault.
sb.verb.new.examples:
sb new book-club "Book Club"	creates <workspace>/book-club
sb new site "Site" --group clients	creates <workspace>/clients/site
sb new --order _orders/ORDER-2026-09-26-book-club.md	from the welcome Pilot's order
sb new site "Site" --ask	also asks the three questions of the project profile
sb.verb.adopt.summary: Adopt a folder you already have
sb.verb.adopt.does:
Writes only what is missing: birth certificate, pointers, Pilot prompt, registry line,
skill links. Records a dated baseline, reports what exists, proposes a reorganisation plan.
sb.verb.adopt.doesNot:
It moves and deletes nothing, and applies no plan. On a project already adopted
it only completes, for instance the links of renamed skills.
sb.verb.adopt.examples:
sb adopt	the current folder
sb adopt ../notes "Notes"	another folder, with its name
sb adopt --git	add Git to a project adopted without it
sb adopt --ask	also asks the three questions of the project profile
sb.verb.list.summary: The projects this Second Brain knows
sb.verb.list.does:
Reads the registry: each project's name, folder, status, version control,
conformity, and the name its Pilot Project must carry.
sb.verb.list.doesNot: It does not open them and checks nothing: sb doctor inside a project does.
sb.verb.pilot-prompt.summary: The block to paste into a project's Pilot Project, or into the welcome one
sb.verb.pilot-prompt.does:
Gives the four pieces a Pilot needs: the Project name, the instructions block
(the common trunk, with this Vault's server), the first message, the canary.
With --accueil (or accueil), anywhere in the workspace: the same pieces for the welcome Pilot
« SB - Accueil », whose block is the one project-bootstrap.sh accueil-prompt prints, with no bash to type;
its first conversation starts with the starting interview.
The block is the same for every host; the steps follow, for each Pilot host present,
or for the one --host names (claude-desktop, codex, gemini, cursor, windsurf, cline, lmstudio).
sb.verb.pilot-prompt.doesNot: It writes nothing, except with --regen, which regenerates state/PILOT-PROMPT.md; --accueil never writes anything.
sb.verb.pilot-prompt.examples:
sb pilot-prompt	the current project
sb pilot-prompt ../book-club	another project
sb pilot-prompt --regen	after a Vault update
sb pilot-prompt --accueil	the welcome Pilot « SB - Accueil », from the workspace
sb pilot-prompt --accueil --host codex	the steps for a Pilot in Codex
sb.verb.mission.summary: Write a Mission (in the Pilot window)
sb.verb.mission.does:
The Pilot checks first whether a light Note is enough; otherwise it writes the Mission
from the template, runs the checklist, and hands you the mini-prompt for the Executor.
sb.verb.mission.doesNot: The Executor never writes its own Mission. Nothing runs before you authorise it.
sb.verb.mission.examples:
sb mission	as a message, in the Pilot window
« écris la Mission »	the former phrasing, same effect
sb.verb.run.summary: Carry out a Mission (in the Executor window)
sb.verb.run.does:
Finds the Mission by its number, shows its authorisation and subject, and the line
to paste; the Executor then opens, checks the preconditions, executes, reports, relays.
sb.verb.run.doesNot:
It does nothing outside the Mission's scope, never pushes without your delegation,
never calls a model unless the Mission allows it.
sb.verb.run.examples:
sb run	the recent Missions
sb run 236	Mission 236 of the current project
/sb:run 236	the same, from Claude Code
sb.verb.relay.summary: Read the RELAY block of the last report
sb.verb.relay.does:
Prints the RELAY section of the newest report of the project, or of the report you name,
ready to carry back to the Pilot.
sb.verb.relay.doesNot: It does not open the whole report: only the verdict or « À trancher » calls for that.
sb.verb.relay.examples:
sb relay	the last report
sb relay reports/REPORT-2026-09-26-183948-235-common-prompt.md	a given report
sb.verb.push.does:
Pushes what your branch has beyond its remote through the verified push: path, current
commit, remote head and history checked first.
sb.verb.push.doesNot: It never forces. An agent pushes only on your delegation, named in its window.
sb.verb.push.examples:
sb push --dry-run	see what would go
sb push	push the current repository
sb push C:/Users/you/Workspaces/vault a1b2c3d..e4f5a6b	a named range
sb.verb.search.summary: Find a document, a rule, a decision, a term
sb.verb.search.does:
Searches the Vault by content, indexes and descriptions first; your agent then
reads what it found before citing a path.
sb.verb.search.doesNot: It never asserts a path that was not measured.
sb.verb.search.examples:
sb search "verified push"	anywhere
sb search handoff --limit 5	the first five
sb.verb.doctor.summary: Check everything, and explain a refusal
sb.verb.doctor.does:
Checks sb on the PATH, Git and uv, bash under Windows, the workspace root, the Vault's guardians and tree,
the Codex budget and its margin, the MCP server in every host present, the Claude Code plugin; in a project, its identity, conformity and links.
Given a refusal message, finds its cause and fix in the guides.
sb.verb.doctor.doesNot: It repairs nothing: each problem comes with the command that fixes it.
sb.verb.doctor.examples:
sb doctor	the full checkup
sb doctor "preflight absent"	what does this refusal mean?
sb.verb.clean.summary: What clutters the workspace, and where it should go
sb.verb.clean.does:
Lists what the workspace root holds beyond its allowed list, and measures the declared
temporary folder and the trash. With --purge-temp, empties the temporary folder after
your confirmation (--yes to skip the question).
sb.verb.clean.doesNot:
It never touches _trash nor _archive, and moves nothing. Emptying the temporary folder
is your gesture: it happens only when you ask for it.
sb.verb.clean.examples:
sb clean	anywhere in the workspace
sb clean --purge-temp	empty the temporary folder, after a question
sb.verb.update.summary: Bring the Vault to a published version
sb.verb.update.does:
Merges the version over your own commits (your profile, your projects' sheets, the registry
stay as they are) and regenerates what is generated.
sb.verb.update.doesNot: It never resolves a conflict behind your back: it refuses by name, with nothing changed.
sb.verb.update.examples: sb update v0.1.15	to that version
sb.verb.install.summary: Install, repair, put sb on the PATH
sb.verb.install.doesNot: It writes nothing into your profile but the PATH entry and Claude Code's own plugin settings, the two things you ask it for.
sb.verb.install.examples:
sb install	the four steps, each only if needed
sb install --plugin	only the Claude Code plugin
sb install --run	resume or repair the installation
sb install --mcp --label acme	the server under a shorter name
sb.verb.uninstall.does: Gives the steps in order, with your paths; --path takes sb off your PATH.
sb.verb.uninstall.doesNot: It deletes nothing: deleting the workspace is your gesture.
sb.verb.uninstall.examples:
sb uninstall	the steps
sb uninstall --path	take sb off the PATH
sb.verb.add-skill.summary: Check a new skill before adding it
sb.verb.add-skill.does: Checks the skill's name and description, and the Codex budget once it is added.
sb.verb.add-skill.doesNot: It copies and links nothing: adding a skill is done under a Mission.
sb.verb.add-skill.examples: sb add-skill ../drafts/meeting-notes	check a skill folder
sb.verb.publish.summary: Publish a version (the maintainer, from the laboratory)
sb.verb.publish.does: Publishes the laboratory Vault to its release remote, in one commit.
sb.verb.publish.doesNot: It refuses in any Vault that is not the laboratory. The tag and its push stay the Owner's gestures.
sb.verb.publish.examples: sb publish --version v0.1.15 --dry-run	check without publishing
